public_rationale: On August 25, 2026, Zitron acknowledged a mistake in his recalled prediction that OpenAI would be dead by the end of 2025 [e2]. OpenAI's January 18, 2026 disclosure describes subscriptions, API services and ongoing customer activity, establishing business operations after that deadline [e1]. The acknowledgment and the evidence of continued operations support the retrospective admission [e1][e2].
limitations: The exact original prediction with an end-of-2025 deadline remains unverified. The related July 29, 2024 article describes a qualified, conditional survival forecast [e3].
Continued operations in January 2026 do not establish long-term financial viability [e1].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The author admits his 2024 prediction that OpenAI would be dead by the end of 2025 was wrong.

statement.excerpt: Sidenote: We all make mistakes. I said OpenAI would be dead by the end of 2025 back in 2024 because I believed that the world would see sense and that hyperscalers wouldn’t just annihilate hundreds of billions more dollars without proof it was worth it.

from_speaker: I said OpenAI would be dead by the end of 2025 back in 2024
our_interpretation: Assess the retrospective admission, not a new forecast of OpenAI's collapse.
The ordinary meaning of 'dead' is that OpenAI ceased operating as a business.
The supplied passage acknowledges a failed prediction. Independent evidence must establish survival beyond 2025.
The target period covers the recalled 2024 prediction through the August 2026 acknowledgment. Verification of the original prediction's exact deadline is a separate provenance question.
criteria.support_condition: The passage acknowledges the failed prediction, and independent records establish that OpenAI continued operating after December 31, 2025.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable records establish that OpenAI ceased operating by December 31, 2025, or the passage does not acknowledge a failed prediction.
